audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers' level charts gave Neeko rows 1-6 ('Skill' x6 then 'Mel'), which contradicts the packet chart (Skill / Mel x5 / Skill), the 47.37% win rate over 19 games, and the already-audited mirror (mel__neeko: 'phases Skill / Mel x5 / Skill').
audit.why: Mel's Radiant Volley (Q, 950 range, 10/9/8/7/6s) and Solar Snare (E, 1000 range, root+slow) both outrange and out-tempo Neeko's 800-range Q, so Mel owns Levels 2 through first item; only Level 1 (one spell each) and the two-item teamfight point are neutral.
audit.corrected: Level 1 Skill, Levels 2 through first item Mel, 2+ items Skill — proposed as matched full/content pairs with ratings dropped to 4/10 on Mel's rows.

audit.why: Spike structure is right: Neeko's real spikes are Level 6 Pop Blossom and Stormsurge; Mel's is her Lost Chapter poke item. The spikes[] array already has all four entries with correct 'when' values.
audit.corrected: Kept the spike timings; corrected only the ability attribution inside spikes[2].text and tightened phases[4]/[5].why to name the barrier and the item lead.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer repeatedly attributes the projectile-reflect to Mel's R ('she holds R to reflect your burst back', 'her R can swallow my whole combo', wants.foe[1] 'Hold R to reflect'). That is flatly the wrong ability.
audit.why: Per the kit, the reflect barrier is Rebuttal (W) — 38/35/33/29/26s cooldown, 250 range, reflects projectiles, prevents damage, grants move speed. Mel's R is Golden Eclipse: a 25000-range global that strikes every Overwhelm-marked enemy and scales with stacks. Telling the player to bait 'her R' before ulting sends them to bait a global they can never see coming, while walking into the actual 26-38s barrier. The mirror audit already established that Rebuttal blanks Pop Blossom's damage but cannot return it and does not stop the stun.
audit.corrected: Rebuttal (W) is the answer to your burst — it makes her damage-immune and bounces your Q seed, but it does NOT stop Pop Blossom's knockup or stun. Bait it, wait the 26s at rank 5, then commit. Separately, Golden Eclipse (R) is global and executes off Overwhelm stacks, so chip damage from lane can kill you off-screen.

audit.why: Rebuttal is 38/35/33/29/26s. Fifteen seconds understates the punish window by more than half and makes the player re-fear a barrier that is still down.

audit.whatIsWrong: Neither layer mentions Mel's Searing Brilliance (P) auto-reset wind-up as the burst tell, and the Rebuttal-absorbs-burst interaction was absent from the content layer.
audit.why: Both were flagged in missingInteractions for this exact matchup.
audit.corrected: The barrier point is now stated in whys[4], spikes[2].text, mid and late. The passive wind-up tell is recorded here but not forced into prose, as no writable field could carry it inside its length band.

edits.before: Through 4-5 she keeps the poke lead — I can't all-in without ult, so I farm with Q and look for a clean E. At 6 Pop Blossom is my one real spike: a landed E into Q into the slam stun can chunk her or force her flash. The trap is her R — it reflects my burst, so if I dump Pop Blossom into a held R I delete myself, not her. I bait it with W's clone/invis or a Q first, then commit. Use disguise to set the ult unseen and roam, because winning this lane straight up against her range is the hard way.
edits.after: Through 4-5 she keeps the poke lead — I can't all-in without ult, so I farm with Q and look for a clean E. At 6 Pop Blossom is my one real spike: a landed Tangle Barbs into Q into the slam stun can chunk her or force Flash. The trap is Rebuttal (W): it makes her damage-immune and bounces my Q seed back, though the stun still lands. I bait the barrier, count its 26 seconds, then commit. Disguise sets the ult unseen — and Golden Eclipse (R) is global, so her Overwhelm stacks execute me off-screen.

edits.before: Late, the lane evens back out only because we're both squishy teamfight casters now — my Pop Blossom into a clustered team can match her execute-and-poke value, and disguise picks are my best path. I don't facecheck her or walk up to a sidelane creep wave alone — I play off my team, land E on her carry, and let the AoE bomb do the work rather than dueling her.
